- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in subsequent periods.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >5% gap), sentiment history suggests bullish reversal; adjust upward by 1–2% for next period.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >5% gap), sentiment history suggests bearish reversal; adjust downward by 1–2% for next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 1–3 periods; apply a 1–2% forward bias adjustment if sentiment is trending upward.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or negative values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 2–4% to compensate for pessimism bias.
